You'll forfeit the round and any chips already in the pot.
Every bet and call this hand stacks into the pot. The player with the best hand at showdown wins it all.
Use them to bet, call, and raise during a hand. Chips you put in go to the pot - the player with the best hand at showdown wins it.
Go bust against bots and a fresh stack arrives next hand. Practice chips don't count for keeps.
That's how many chips they've added to the pot on this betting round. It resets when the next card hits the board.
Action moves clockwise from the player left of the dealer. The dealer position rotates each hand.
Forced half-bet, posted by the player immediately left of the dealer before any cards are dealt.
Forced full bet, posted left of the small blind. The minimum opening bet for the hand.
Fold means giving up the hand. Any chips already in the pot stay there - they don't come back.
Check passes the action without putting any chips in. Only legal when there's nothing to call.
Call matches the current bet so they can stay in the hand. No raise, just keeping up.
Bet opens the betting on this street. Everyone else now has to call, raise, or fold.
Raise increases the current bet. Everyone else who wants to stay in has to match the new total.
All in means pushing their entire stack into the pot. They can't act again this hand.
Tap the ? icon up top for the full list of actions.
Ten through Ace, all the same suit. The strongest hand in poker.
Five cards in a row, all the same suit. Above four of a kind.
Four cards of the same rank. Beats every hand except a straight flush or royal flush.
Three of a kind plus a pair. Beats a flush.
Five cards of the same suit, in any order. Beats a straight.
Five cards in a row, mixed suits. Beats three of a kind.
Three cards of the same rank. Beats two pair.
Two pairs of different ranks. Beats a single pair.
Your two hole cards are the same rank - already a pair before any community cards. Strong starting hand.
Two cards of the same rank. Beats a high card.
No combinations - the highest single card wins. The weakest hand category.
Your current hand, based on your hole cards and what's on the board.
Tap the ? icon up top for the full ranking list with examples.
Practice chips refilled - chips against bots don't count for keeps. Deal yourself in and keep sharpening up.
You've busted out of this game. Rebuy to jump back in, or leave the table.
Top up without leaving the table.
Pass to the next player without betting.
Match the current bet to stay in the hand.
Increase the current bet. Everyone else must call, raise, or fold.
Give up the hand. Any chips already in the pot stay.
Push your entire stack. If you win, you win up to what everyone matched.
Two cards dealt face-down to each player. Blinds are posted; players act starting left of the big blind. Fold, call, or raise.
Three community cards revealed. Combine any two of your hole cards with the board (or play the board) to make your best 5-card hand. A new round of betting begins.
Fourth community card on the board. One more round of betting before the river - bets typically get bigger here.
Fifth and final community card. One last round of betting, then any remaining players show their cards.
All remaining players reveal their hands. Best 5-card hand using any combination of hole and community cards wins the pot.
Hand finished - chips are being awarded. Tap "Next hand" to play again.
You won't see their table blasts.

Bots only see their own hand and the community cards. They don't use AI - each follows a fixed heuristic playing style.

Plays a wide range and bets confidently. Pushes hard when they sense weakness.
Patient, but when chips go in, expect a real hand.
Folds often, rarely raises. A big bet from this seat usually means the goods.
Calls a lot, rarely raises. Hard to push off marginal hands - value bet, don't bluff.
Mixes it up. No single tendency to exploit - read each hand.
Forgiving table. Bots play loosely and rarely punish a thin call - a good place to find your footing.
Balanced challenge. Bots punish loose play and exploit obvious tells - the default test of your read.
Sharp table. Bots pressure marginal hands and read your patterns - bring your A game.

You are playing our bots while we find you real opponents - and we mean it: beat them and you keep the chips you win, on the house, up to a daily limit.
Skip basics, I know how to play
Every hand, players bet chips into a shared pot. Win the hand and you take it all, either by having the best cards at showdown, or by getting everyone else to fold first.
Your hand is your two cards combined with five shared cards on the table. The strongest five-card combination wins. We'll show you the ranking in-game whenever you need it.
Three things to do on your turn.
When it's your action, you have three choices. Fold and you're out. Call to stay in. Raise to put pressure on. That's the whole game, done thousands of different ways.
Meet Ada, Ben, and Cleo. They're bots. Tap anything on this screen if you're curious; most things will tell you what they are. Tap your cards and they flip to show their backs.
Ada has the small blind (10), Ben the big blind (20). Two forced bets that start every hand and seed the pot. They rotate left each hand so everyone takes turns posting.
Best starting hand in poker. A raise builds the pot when you're strong, but raise too big and opponents fold rather than pay you off.
Tap Raise to put chips in. The ↑ opens a sheet for sizing the bet; the button itself raises the minimum.
Each player's last move shows next to their seat. The pot ticked up.
Decent hand: same suit, both high cards. Straight, flush, even a royal flush are all on the table. 10 chips to call and see the flop.
Two hearts on the flop plus your two: one more heart and you've made a flush. Ada checked, so you can see the next card free. Tap Check.
Turn brought another heart, you made your flush. Ada folded along the way, so the pot is yours. Most hands end like this, not at showdown.
Tap ↑ then Fold, or swipe up on your cards. Either works.
Tap anything on a real table you're not sure about; most things will explain themselves. Bots are waiting in Practice.
